item.title: Trump claims ‘active’ peace talks with Iran as bombing deadline approaches
item.summary: The president has given Iranian officials until 8 p.m. Tuesday to make a ceasefire deal or face widespread destruction. Tehran on Monday reasserted its rejection of U.S. demands.

item.title: Kidnapped U.S. journalist believed alive in militia’s Iraqi stronghold
item.summary: U.S. and Iraqi officials say they believe freelancer Shelly Kittleson was kidnapped last week by Kataib Hezbollah, a paramilitary group with links to Iran.

item.title: Trump threatens new rampage as Iran deal deadline nears
item.summary: The president vowed anew to destroy Iranian bridges and energy sites if a deal to open the Strait of Hormuz isn’t reached.

item.title: From Oman, a waterfront view of the embattled Strait of Hormuz
item.summary: Residents of Khasab, a sleepy exclave that depends on fishing and tourism, are frustrated by the war in Iran and fearful of what’s next.

item.title: China stands to benefit most from the war-driven energy crisis
item.summary: Sales of Chinese electric vehicles and solar panels have surged since the start of the Iran war, companies say.

item.title: On Easter, Pope Leo delivers commanding message of peace to a world at war
item.summary: “Let those who have weapons lay them down!” the first American pope declared. The White House’s war in Iran and nativist agenda at home are testing the Vatican.

item.title: It’s Holy Week, but Jerusalem’s Old City is quiet and eerily empty
item.summary: The Austrian Hospice urges groups of Christian pilgrims to book 16 months ahead. One night this week, a receptionist warned a Post reporter she would be the only guest.

item.title: Trump threatens Iran with ‘Hell’ over Strait of Hormuz in profane post
item.summary: Trump escalated threats against Iran’s power plants, bridges and other infrastructure in an expletive-laden post on Truth Social on Easter morning.

item.title: Trump administration’s secrecy on health deals alarms experts, governments
item.summary: A dearth of information has been disclosed about the agreements, fueling speculation that the “America First” approach to foreign aid is exploitative.
